_comment: Per-asset settings for tools/run_chunk_pass.py. Two shading families: 'faceted' keeps crisp planes for hard-surface props, 'smooth' is for anything that should read as a rounded mass. Organics are smooth -- planarise and hardened bevel normals turn a dome into a dented polyhedron, and no amount of normal work hides that. Smooth assets need real density too, so they subdivide; the reference for 'right' is prop_firepit_polished.

excluded.prop_leafy_bush: Not salvageable by this pass. The generated shell has real holes through it and spike protrusions, so smoothing and relaxing only shrink the mass while the holes stay -- relax 0.60, 0.75, and 0.85 were all tried. Per ASSET_PIPELINE.md this needs regenerating or hand-authoring, not automatic deformation. prop_bush_a/b/c are hand-built and already measure inside the coherent band (facet_evenness 0.045), so one of those, or a KayKit forest bush, is the stand-in until it is redone.

prop_fir.note: Tall, thin, many wafer tiers. Squat it hard and hide the spiky root star under the canopy. Its visible stem is canopy geometry, not the 107-face Trunk mesh, so recolour it by radius.

prop_stone_pine.note: Already broad, so widen gently; the trunk is the heavy read here.

prop_shrooms.note: Arrived as droopy hooked wizard hats. The dome stage conforms each cap to a round Garden Galaxy silhouette; widen/squash are left alone because the dome already sets cap proportions. Subdivide 2 reads marginally cleaner but costs 48k triangles for a decoration; 1 plus a heavier relax lands at 12k.
